rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE IMPOSITION BY THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT OF AN IDLE LAND TAX, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE THE PERTINENT PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Studies on local finance show that the idle land tax is not being implemented by local government units due to certain operational difficulties. It is believed that if the national government were to impose the idle land tax, local officials will most likely implement the same. The bill seeks to provide for the imposition by the national government of a 10% idle land tax based on the zonal value or the fair market value of the land, whichever is higher.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE TAX ON IDLE LANDS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE, SECTION 236 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Of the country's total land area of 30 million hectares, around 14.12 hectares are classified as alienable and disposable. Had these lands been utilized, agricultural productivity and food security would not be a critical problem today. This measure seeks to increase the ceiling of the tax on idle lands from 5% to 10% to give local government units more flexibility in its imposition. The current maximum tax of 5% has not proven to be an effective deterrent against the non-utilization of agricultural lands for productive purposes.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS TO APPROPRIATE 10% OF THEIR DEVELOPMENT FUNDS TO SUPPORT THE SOCIAL REFORM AGENDA, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 324 OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The annual budgets of local government units are heavily focused on infrastructure development programs leaving social services and other development programs a second priority. This bill seeks to approximate an equal allotment of local government resources by requiring municipalities, cities and provinces to appropriate not less than 10% of annual development funds to support programs under the ambit of the Social Reform Agenda.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE AUTOMATIC RELEASE OF THE SHARE OF THE BARANGAY IN THE PROCEEDS OF NATIONAL TAXES AND TAXES ON THE UTILIZATION AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE NATIONAL WEALTH, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTION 286, CHAPTER 1 AND SECTION 293, CHAPTER 2, TITLE 3, BOOK II, RESPECTIVELY, OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The government is in the process of redistributing power, resources and services from the central government to lower level political communities. However, in many cases, the local officials hold the barangays hostage by withholding the release of their share. The bill provides that the share of the barangays shall not be subject to any lien or holdback that may be imposed by the provincial, city or municipal government for whatever purpose.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT THE SCHEDULE OF FAIR MARKET VALUES OF REAL PROPERTY SHALL BE PREPARED BY THE LOCAL ASSESSMENT COUNCIL AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: At present, the preparation of the schedule of fair market values of real property is the sole responsibility of the provincial, city or municipal assessor. Instead of one person performing such function, it is suggested that the function be assigned to a collegial body. This bill seeks to empower the local assessment council to prepare the schedule of fair market values of real property to eliminate the possibility of drawing up a schedule which favors certain groups of sectors or is erroneously done.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING LOCAL FISCAL AUTONOMY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Various opinions rendered by national government agencies have unduly restricted the utilization of local government funds by the local government units (LGUs). This bill seeks to strengthen  the fiscal autonomy of LGU in terms of disposition, allocation and utilization of local government funds from whatever source. It also aims to increase the share of LGUs in internal revenue taxes and other national taxes and fees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION TWO HUNDRED TWENTY OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE,' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Local Government Code granted the Sanggunians the authority to pass an ordinance increasing the assessment value of real property as basis in computing the real estate tax (residential, agricultural, commercial and industrial lands) once every three years. This provision has been viewed as unfair and prejudicial to taxpayers because it unduly burdens the owners of residential properties. This bill seeks to protect the owners of residential property from excessive real estate assessments by limiting the duration wherein a reassessment can be made to every ten years.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE TRANSFER OF ANCESTRAL LAND BELONGING TO THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLE TO NON-MEMBERS, AMENDING SECTION 8 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8371, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Prohibiting the Transfer of Ancestral Land Belonging to the Indigenous People to Non-Members
rows.abstract: RA 8371 (Indigenous Peoples' Act) does not clearly state whether the sale of ancestral lands by a member of the indigenous cultural communities (ICCs) and indigenous people to a non-member is allowed or not. In the absence of a clear prohibition, it is feared that our ancestral lands will be dissipated gradually. This bill seeks to remove the ambiguity in the law by amending RA 8371 to clearly prohibit the sale of ancestral lands by a member of the ICCs to a non-member.
rows.status: Business for the day on 2006-09-27

rows.author: C020
rows.mother_status: Business for the day on 2006-11-27
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVEN THOUSAND NINE HUNDRED FORTY-ONE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS 'THE PARTY-LIST SYSTEM ACT'
rows.abstract: RA 7941 failed to address the following concerns: 1) the procedure in allocating seats for party-list representatives; and 2) the liberal interpretation which allow mainstream political parties and organizations and non-marginalized sectors to join and participate in the party-list elections. This bill seeks to propose the following: a) a mechanism that will bridge the gap in the existing law; and b) disallow mainstream political parties and non-marginalized sectors from participating in the party-list elections.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05876

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A CEILING ON ALL PUBLIC DEBTS OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Public Debt Ceiling Act of 2004\". In view of the ballooning public debt of the national government, this bill seeks to impose a debt cap or debt ceiling so as not to hamper the delivery of basic social services and other priority concerns of the government to the detriment of public interest.  It sets the total public debt ceiling at PhP1.2 trillion
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED SIX HUNDRED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE MARINE POLLUTION DECREE OF 1974
rows.abstract: This measure seeks to increase the penalty for the unlawful dumping of wastes and other matters that create hazards to human health, harm living resources and marine life, damages amenities or interfere with the legitimate uses of the sea. It holds the head of a corporation or any partnership culpable for violations of the provisions of the proposed measure. It defines the guidelines under which the Philippine Coast Guard may allow the dumping of waste materials. It likewise,authorizes the adoption of a dumping system.
rows.status: Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2005-01-27

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2004-09-15
Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2005-01-27

rows.author: C020
rows.mother_status: Business for the day on 2005-08-10
rows.title_full: AN ACT TOTALLY BANNING LOGGING OPERATIONS FOR THE NEXT 25 YEARS
rows.abstract: Our forests are being denuded at an alarming rate. In order to save our remaining forests and to ensure the successful reforestation of badly denuded areas, the measure proposes to impose a total log ban in forests, timberlands, forest reserves and watersheds for the next 25 years.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04431

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROMOTION OF BIO-ORGANIC FARMING IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: The adoption of bio-organic farming methods not only helps to reduce pollution and abate the destruction of useful organisms for the agricultural ecosystem, it also helps to solve the problem of waste and garbage disposal through the use of plant and animal waste and crop residues.
rows.status: Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2005-03-15

Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2005-03-15

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT BANNING FISH CULTURE PENS IN LAKES THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to prohibit the construction of fish culture pens in lakes and tributaries  throughout the country. It also authorizes the summary abatement of existing ones as nuisance per set by the local government units that have jurisdiction over the fish culture pens concerned at the expense of the owners thereof without prejudice to their criminal liability.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AQUACULTURE AND FISHERIES RESOURCES since 2005-01-12

rows.title_full: AN ACT URGING THE PRESIDENT AND THE OFFICIALS OF THE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES TO DECLARE A TOTAL LOG BAN IN THE THIRD DISTRICT OF THE PROVINCE OF NEGROS OCCIDENTAL, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.status: Substituted by HB04483

rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING A FARMER-BENEFICIARY TO MORTAGE HIS RIGHT TO FARM LAND AWARDED TO HIM, WITHOUT LOSING HIS SECURITY TO TENURE AND PROVIDING THAT THE CERTIFICATE OF LAND OWNERSHIP AWARD ISSUED TO HIM UNDER THE COMPREHENSIVE AGRARIAN REFORM PROGRAM SHALL BE ACCEPTED BY BANKS AND OTHER FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS AS COLLATERAL FOR LOANS AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS TWENTY-SEVEN AND TWENTY-ONE OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-SIX HUNDRED AND FIFTY SEVEN, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'COMPREHENSIVE AGRARIAN REFORM LAW OF 1998,' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to allow farmer-beneficiaries of the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Law (CARL) to use awarded land as collateral in availing of both short-term and long-term production and other types of loans from commercial banks  and other financial institutions for the acquisition of farm equipment and machineries, seeds, fertilizers and other similar items and to allow foreclosure of collateral in case of loan payment default by debtor and re-sale to the Land Bank in the amount equivalent to the unpaid portion of the loan plus interest. It provides that the farmer-beneficiary shall neither lose his security of tenure nor be ejected from the land within the mortgage period provided he regularly pays the amortization.
rows.status: Approved by the Committee on Ways and Means on 2005-08-16

committee_action.action: Approved by the Committee on Ways and Means on 2005-08-16

rows.title_full: AN ACT REORGANIZING THE NATIONAL FOOD AUTHORITY INTO THE NATIONAL FOOD CORPORATION AND THE FOOD DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATORY ADMINISTRATION, REDEFINING THEIR POWERS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: National Food Authority Reorganization Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"National Food Authority Reorganization Act of 2003\" The National Food Authority (NFA) is mandated to ensure food security in staple cereals in times and places of natural and man-made calamity. For the NFA to be truly effective, this bill seeks to strengthen the NFA financially and structurally. It aims to institute reforms in administration and reorganize the NFA into the National Food Corporation attached to the Office of the President.
rows.status: Approved by the Committee on 2006-09-26

Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2006-09-26

Transmitted to Cttee. on Appropriations (2005-8-15).  Substitute bill approved during the Executive Session by the Cttees. on Gov't. Enterprises & Privatization and Reorganization(2005-8-3).

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE INCLUSION OF ALL ELECTRIC COOPERATIVES ORGANIZED AND EXISTING UNDER PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 269, AS AMENDED, AND REGISTERED WITH THE NATIONAL ELECTRIFICATION ADMINISTRATION (NEA) WITHIN THE COVERAGE OF TAX EXEMPTION PRIVILEGES AND INCENTIVES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Sections 193 and 234 of the Local Government Code (LGC) effectively withdrew the tax exemption benefits enjoyed by electric cooperatives. The withdrawal of the incentive caused electric cooperatives to suffer heavy financial losses. This bill seeks to exempt electric cooperatives from the payment of real property taxes and other fees imposed by the local government units. It seeks to include all electric cooperatives organized under PD 269, as amended, and registered with the National Electrification Administration, within the coverage of tax exemption privileges and incentives granted under the LGC.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING FROM WITHHOLDING TAX THE INTEREST EARNINGS ON BONDS ISSUED BY THE LANDBANK OF THE PHILIPPINES TO LANDOWNERS ON THE SALE OF THEIR LANDS COVERED BY THE COMPREHENSIVE AGRARIAN REFORM LAW
rows.abstract: To hasten payment to landowners covered by the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Law (CARL) and to maintain the financial viability of the Land Bank (LBP), one of the modes of compensation to landowners was in the form of LBP bonds bearing interest subject to withholding tax. This bill seeks to exempt from the withholding tax all interest earnings on bonds issued by the LBP to landowners for the sale of their lands covered by the CARL to give landowners some relief from their financial burdens.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVING FOR THE UPGRADING OF THE RATES OF COMPENSATION OF THE OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES OF THE JUDICIARY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"Judiciary Compensation Restructure Act of 2003\". The Judiciary Compensation Act granted special monthly allowances to justices and judges only. This resulted in widespread demoralization among the ranks of court officers and employees who perform the bulk of tasks needed in the dispensation of justice. This bill seeks to provide for the upgrading of the rates of compensation of the officers and employees of the Philippine judiciary.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR SCHOOLS, COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES WHICH REFUSE ADMISSION OF QUALIFIED SCHOLARS OF THE PHILIPPINE VETERANS AFFAIRS OFFICE
rows.abstract: The bill  seeks to penalize schools that refuse enrolment of qualified Philippine Veterans Office scholars due to non-payment of school bills, with a fine at P10,000.00 for the 1st offense, P20,000.00 for the 2nd offense and P50,000.00 for the 3rd offense.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT SEPARATING VICTORIAS NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL BARANGAY ESTADO EXTENSION HIGH SCHOOL IN BARANGAY ESTADO, CITY OF VICTORIAS, FROM VICTORIAS NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL, VICTORIAS CITY, AND CONVERTING IT INTO AN INDEPENDENT NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE POSITION OF BARANGAY POPULATION WORKER, GRANTING BENEFITS THERETO, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE 'LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991', AS AMENDED, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The Barangay Population Worker shall be tasked to conduct studies on reproductive technologies currently in use; and collect, analyze and disseminate basic data on population principles and development.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A BARANGAY NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL IN THE CITY OF TALISAY, PROVINCE OF NEGROS OCCIDENTAL, TO BE KNOWN AS THE BARANGAY EFEGENIO LIZARES NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO STABILIZE THE SUGAR INDUSTRY BY ESTABLISHING THE SUGAR INDUSTRY RESEARCH AND STABILIZATION FUND AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Since its creation, the programs of the Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) have suffered setbacks due to lack of funds.  The bill seeks to provide the SRA with adequate funding to enable it to pursue and carry out its mandate by requiring that 20% of the value-added tax collections on sugar and its by-products be channeled back to the sugar industry.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ADJUSTMENTS IN THE MONTHLY CONTRIBUTIONS OF PHILHEALTH MEMBERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY EIGHT HUNDRED AND SEVENTY FIVE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'NATIONAL HEALTH INSURANCE ACT OF 1995,' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: At present, the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (Philhealth) covers only 5% to 10% of the total hospitalization expenses of its member. This bill seeks to adjust the monthly contributions of Philhealth members to increase the funds of Philhealth and consequently allow for a more reasonsble coverage in case a member is hospitalized.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE USE OF UNLEADED GASOLINE AS FUEL IN ALL LAND TRANSPORTS MOTOR VEHICLES
rows.abstract: \"Unleaded Gasoline Use Act of 2003\". Lead is a major environmental health hazard. The bill seeks the mandatory use of unleaded gasoline as fuel in all land transport motor vehicles. Unleaded gasoline is a clearer fuel than diesel or leaded gasoline and is estimated to be cheaper compared to the prices of other petroleum products prevailing in the market.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2006-09-20

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2006-09-20

rows.title_full: AN ACT CONVERTING THE NEGROS OCCIDENTAL SCIENCE HIGH SCHOOL TO NATIONAL SCIENCE HIGH SCHOOL IN THE CITY OF VICTORIAS, PROVINCE OF NEGROS OCCIDENTAL, TO BE KNOWN AS THE NEGROS OCCIDENTAL NATIONAL SCIENCE HIGH SCHOOL AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Substituted by HB05813

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 717, ENTITLED 'PROVIDING AN AGRARIAN REFORM CREDIT AND FINANCING SYSTEM FOR AGRARIAN REFORM BENEFICIARIES THROUGH BANKING INSTITUTIONS'
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to correct the decline in agricultural production loans by redirecting the Agri-Agra Fund's use to favor small farmers. The enactment of the measure is expected to result in the infusion of more than PhP 100.0 billion into the countryside over the next two years. The bill will dramatically reduce rural poverty that has shackled the country for centuries.
rows.status: Scheduled for first meeting/hearing on 2006-08-29

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SYSTEM OF DISPOSITION OF SEIZED/CONFISCATED ILLEGALY CUT, GATHERED, REMOVED, AND POSSESSED LOGS, LUMBER, FLITCHES, AND OTHER FOREST PRODUCTS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: System of Disposition of Seized/Confiscated Illegally Cut, Gathered, Removed and Possessed Logs and Other Forest Products
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to prohibit the auctioning of seized/confiscated illegally cut, gathered, removed or processed logs, lumber, flitches and other forest products by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) through the Natural Resources Development Corporation. It provides a system whereby the DENR shall dispose and apportion confiscated forest products.

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE DESIGNATION OF A ONE METER WIDE LANE FOR THE EXCLUSIVE USE OF BICYCLE RIDERS IN ALL NATIONAL ROADS OF THE COUNTRY, PRESCRIBING THE PENALTY FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to create a bicycle lane in designated roads so as to provide biking enthusiasts a safe and well-deserved byway where they can pass without obstruction or danger from vehicular traffic. A successful promotion of biking as a means of mass transport will bring about a healthy populace free from respiratory ailments and will drastically cut fuel expenses. It will also declog the streets from too much traffic.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE DEPARTMENT OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY TO PROVIDE EVERY BARANGAY TEN (10) PIECES OF STANDARDIZED METAL WEIGHTS WEIGHING ONE (1) KILOGRAM EACH TO BE PUT UNDER THE CUSTODY OF THE BARANGAY CAPTAIN AND LOANED FOR FREE TO ANY BARANGAY RESIDENT WHO WISHES TO CHECK THE ACCURACY OF THE WEIGHING SCALE BEING USED IN THE MARKETING OF ANY PRODUCT WHICH PRICE IS DETERMINED BY WEIGHT AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Despite efforts by the Department of Trade and Industry, unscrupulous sellers and traders still manipulate their weighing scales to make a commodity appear to weigh more or weigh less. To ensure that the weighing instruments being used in the trade are \"honest\", this bill proposes to provide every barangay 10 units of standardized metal weighing instrument weighing one kilogram each to be kept under the custody of the barangay captain and loaned for free to any barangay resident.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE PUBLICATION OF LEWD PHOTOGRAPHS AND SEX STORIES AND ARTICLES IN TABLOID AND BROADSHEET NEWSPAPERS, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to prohibit the publication of lewd photographs and articles in tabloids and broadsheet newspapers. Lewd materials should be kept away from the easy perusal and consumption of the yuoung to ensure a sane and sexually and morally-sound citizenry.
rows.status: Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2005-05-20

committee_action.action: Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2005-05-20

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: CARPARK REGULATION LAW OF 2004
rows.abstract: The non-availability of ample and safe parking spaces has become a perennial problem for motorists and car owners in practically all government agencies and commercial establishments. This bill seeks to regulate the operation of carparks to assure the public of free and easy access to parking spaces. It will also guarantee that vehicles will be well-protected and free from any attempt of theft and other premeditated damages.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

principal_referral.committee: INDIGENOUS CULTURAL COMMUNITIES AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT ENSURING SECURITY OF TENURE FOR AGRARIAN REFORM BENEFICIARIES OVER LANDS AWARDED TO THEM UNDER THE COMPREHENSIVE AGRARIAN REFORM PROGRAM, PROVIDING GUIDELINES FOR THE CANCELLATION OF LAND OWNERSHIP AWARDS, PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The rampant cancellation of Emancipation Patents (EPs) and Certificates of Land Ownership Awards (CLOAs) issued to farmer-beneficiaries under the land reform program has become alarming. The cancellations occur mainly because the subject pieces of land were erroneously covered by the program. This bill seeks to reaffirm that EPSs and CLOAs are land titles under PD 1527. The measure provides for compensation to landowners whose lands were erroneously covered by the land reform program. It ensures that the farmer-beneficiaries do not bear the consequences of the Department of Agrarian Reform's errors in distributing lands that should have been exempted from the coverage of the program.
rows.status: Approved by the Committee on Ways and Means on 2005-08-16

committee_action.action: Approved by the Committee on Ways and Means on 2005-08-16

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE GEOGRAPHICAL REQUIREMENTS IN THE BIDDING AND AWARDING OF CONTRACTS FOR GOVERNMENT INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1594
rows.abstract: In addition to the legal, technical and financial prequalification requirements of prospective contractors spelled out in PD 1594, the bill prescribes certain geographical requirements such that project contractors based in Luzon may only be qualified to undertake government infrastructure projects within Luzon. The same requirement shall apply to contractors based in the Visayas and Mindanao.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PENSION PAY OF FILIPINO AMATEUR ATHLETES WHO HAVE WON MEDALS IN THE OLYMPIC GAMES AND PROFESSIONAL FILIPINO ATHLETES WHO HAVE WON WORLD TITLES OR CHAMPIONSHIPS IN DULY RECOGNIZED AND SANCTIONED PROFESSIONAL INTERNATIONAL SPORTING COMPETITIONS
rows.abstract: Too often, we hear stories of Filipino former star athletes who brought honor and glory to the country only to succumb to poverty and obscurity in their old age. To duly recognize the sacrifices and efforts of old Filipino sports icons, this bill proposes the grant of a monthly pension to all Filipino athletes who, in the past, copped medals in the Olympic Games and won world titles or championships in duly recognized international professional sports competition.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT UPGRADING THE SALARY GRADE LEVEL OF THE SCHOOLS DISTRICT SUPERVISORS FROM SALARY GRADE NINETEEN (19) TO SALARY GRADE TWENTY-FOUR (24)
rows.abstract: It is highly anomalous for a subordinate to receive a much higher compensation than his superior. This is exactly the case between Schools District Supervisors (SDS) and Principals or School Heads whose respective salary grades (SG) are SG 19 and SG 21. This bill seeks to correct the anomaly by upgrading the salary grade level of SDS from SG 19 to SG 24. This will give SDS compensation commensurate to their duties and responsibilities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8189 ENTITLED, 'AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A GENERAL REGISTRATION OF VOTERS, ADOPTING A SYSTEM OF CONTINUING REGISTRATION, PRESCRIBING THE PROCEDURES THEREOF AND AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR' BY DELETING SECTION 44 THEREOF
rows.abstract: Section 44 of RA 8189 mandates the reassignment of election officers every four years to a new station outside of the congressional district they presently serve. The provision is viewed to be onerous since it dislocates their families, affects the schooling of their children and entails additional expenses in establishing a new residence. This bill seeks to delete Section 44and revert back to Article 7, Section 56 of the Omnibus Election Code as the operative rule governing the reassignment of elections officers.
rows.status: Measure reconsidered on 2006-12-20

second_reading.reasons: To enable Rep. Lagman to interpellate the Sponsor on the measure.

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-05-29, transmitted to on 2006-05-31 and received by the Senate on 2006-05-31
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING REAL ESTATE DEVELOPERS TO PLANT AT LEAST FIFTY (50) SHADY TREES FOR EVERY HECTARE OF THE SUBDIVISION PROJECT THEY ARE DEVELOPING AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: The bill proposes to require real estate developers to plant at least 50 shady trees per hectare of the subdivision/residential areas they are developing. This will provide ecological balance and add up to the aesthetic appearance of the place. It will also greatly help in preventing natural disasters such as flooding and landslides.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04074

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATORILY CREATING THE POSITION OF THE MUNICIPAL GENERAL SERVICES OFFICER, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE BOOK III, TITLE TWO, CHAPTER 2, SECTION 443 (a) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The bill proposes the mandatory creation of the position of Municipal General Services Officer to guarantee uniformity of general services management in the provincial, city and municipal levels. The creation of the position would ensure fast delivery of services requiring general services expertise and technical support services. It will also serve to provide an improved system of procurement, care utilization, custody and disposal of supplies and properties of the local government unit.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING ALL OFFICIAL NON-WORKING DAYS TO FALL EITHER ON A MONDAY OR A FRIDAY (House passed its Senate version (SB02119) on Feb. 07, 2007)
rows.title_short: Declaring All Official Non-Working Days to Fall Either on a Monday or a Friday
rows.abstract: It has been observed that when a holiday falls on a Tuesday, employees tend to be absent on the Monday preceding the Tuesday holiday and on the Friday following the Thursday holiday. This bill proposes that all official non-working holidays be mandatorily scheduled to be observed on either a Monday of a Friday. This bill aims to solve the problem of \"intentional absenteeism\" among workers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-07-27
rows.remarks: House passed its Senate version (SB02119) on Feb. 07, 2007.

third_reading.remarks: On Feb. 07, 2007, House concurred with the Senate version (SB02119).

rows.author: D062
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A PHILIPPINE MARITIME AND OCEANS POLICY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Philippine Oceans Act of 2000\". In line with the State's policy to protect the nation's maritime wealth in its archipelagic waters and territorial seas, the bill seeks to institutionalize a maritime and oceans policy. It proposes the adoption of a five-year oceans development agenda covering these programs; a) Philippine oceans information system; b) coastal community capability enhancement of the oceans; c) ocean law and administration reforms; d) environmentally sustainable marine resource management; e) archipelagic development planning program; and f) oceans diplomacy
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D062
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING STIFFER PENALTIES ON ILLEGAL GAMBLING, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED SIXTEEN HUNDRED AND TWO, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Illegal gambling, directly or indirectly, is perceived to be the reason for rise in social ills. The penalties imposed under the present laws have become inadequate to discourage gambling. The bill seeks to increase the penalties for illegal gambling to make it more effective in stopping this social menace which has fostred wrong values and false hopes among countrymen.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D062
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING STIFFER PENALTIES ON PHARMACIES AND DRUG STORES WHICH REFUSE TO HONOR SENIOR CITIZEN CARD ISSUED BY THE GOVERNMENT
rows.abstract: It has been noted that most pharmacies and drugstores refuse to grant the 20% discount for the purchase of medicines by the elderly as mandated under RA 7432. Some drugstores require a written authorization for purchases made by their representative. This bill seeks to impose stiffer penalties on pharmacies and drugstores which refuse to honor the senior citizen card issued by the government to senior citizens who wish to avail of the benefits and privileges granted under RA 7432.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D062
rows.title_full: AN ACT CONSOLIDATING THE MAPPING FUNCTION AND BUDGET UNDER THE OFFICE OF THE NATIONAL MAPPING AND RESOURCE INFORMATION AUTHORITY (NAMRIA)
rows.abstract: Despite the creation of the National Mapping and Resource Information Authority (NAMRIA) which serves as the central mapping agency of the government, it has been observed that some government agencies still do their own mapping services resulting in the duplication efforts and costs. Considering that the NAMRIA is well equipped to handle the job, this bill seeks to consolidate the mapping budget of various departments of the government and centralize such function under the office of the NAMRIA.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D062
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING DISCRIMINATION AGAINST WORK APPLICANTS
rows.abstract: When recruiting new employees, some private companies impose certain requirements that, for some, are almost impossible to comply. Examples of these discriminatory requirements are height, age, skin color and other physical attributes. To promote fairness, equality and justice in employment opportunities, the bill seeks to penalize employers who discriminate against a person for an opportunity to be employed by reason of non-related work requirements.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D062
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING MALL AND STORE OWNERS ENGAGING IN THE SALE OF CONTRABAND PRODUCTS
rows.abstract: Smuggled and pirated goods not only distort normal pricing mechanisms but also affect other market forces that contribute to the decline of the local economy. This bill seeks to clamp down on these illegal activities by penalizing store/stall owners who engage in the selling of contraband products. It also provide penalties for mall owners who tolerate the selling of contraband products by their tenants.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D050
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE CAPABILITY OF THE BUREAU OF FOOD AND DRUGS (BFAD) BY ESTABLISHING ADEQUATE TESTING LABORATORIES AND FIELD OFFICES IN ALL PROVINCES AND CITIES, UPGRADING ITS EQUIPMENT, CREATING A DRUG ENFORCEMENT UNIT (DEU) UNDER ITS OPERATIONAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE CONTROL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"BFAD Empowerment Act of 2004\" The Bureau of Food and Drugs (BFAD) is tasked to ensure the quality of medicines and pharmaceuticals made available to the public. This bill seeks to introduce major reforms in the BFAD to strengthen the capability of the BFAD's regulatory functions of licensing, registration and monitoring. It provides for the augmentation of existing laboratories and the upgrading of their equipment. It also proposes the creation of a drug enforcement unit under its operation and administrative control.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D050
rows.title_full: AN ACT LIMITING THE BORROWING POWER OF THE PRESIDENT BY PRESCRIBING CERTAIN REQUIREMENTS FOR ALL FORMS OF FOREIGN AND DOMESTIC INDEBTEDNESS AND ALL MATTERS RELATING TO THE COUNTRY'S DEBT MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill provides for the prior approval of the Philippine Congress in negotiating and contracting any loan, whether foreign or domestic, in the name and liability of the national government, including those undertaken by government-owned and controlled corporations and local government units.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D050
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE JOINT LEGISLATIVE-EXECUTIVE NATIONAL DEBT COORDINATING COUNCIL OF THE PHILIPPINES (NDCCP) TO ASSIST THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT IN INSTITUTING REFORMS AND DIRECTIONS IN THE COUNTRY'S FOREIGN DEBT POLICY
rows.abstract: This bill calls for a more active participation of Congress in contracting loans in the name of the national government and in negotiations of all matters related to it. It proposes the creation of the Joint Legislative-Executive National Debt Coordinating Council of the Philippines (NDCCP) to assist the national government in the formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of foreign debt management strategies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D050
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MANDATORY AUTOPSY OF ANY PERSON WHO DIED IN A VIOLENT, SUSPICIOUS, QUESTIONABLE, UNUSUAL AND/OR UNNATURAL MANNER, THE CONDITIONS FOR THE PROPER ISSUANCE OF THE DEATH CERTIFICATE OF SAID PERSON AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Autopsy Act of 2004\". The bill requires the conduct of a mandatory professional forensic autopsy in cases of violent, unnatural, questionable, mysterious or unusual death of a person. It also addresses the problem of deficient or inadequate autopsy and post-mortem reports that contribute to the non-prosecution or dismissal of complaints because of the absence or lack of guidelines in the conduct and preparation of the same.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D050
rows.mother_status: Printed copies distributed to members on 2007-06-04
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8293, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, TO LOWER THE COST OF DRUGS AND PHARMACEUTICAL PRODUCTS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: One of the impediments to the implementation of the Generics Law is that drug manufacturers have to wait for a long period for the patent of medicines to expire before they are allowed to manufacture low-priced drugs. To enable the government to control the prevailing price schemes of drug companies and to support the fledging local drug industry, the bill seeks to shorten the patent period of drugs and to institutionalize compulsory licensing.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06035

rows.author: D050
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE REGULATORY POWER OF THE STATE AND THE POSITION AND COMPETITIVENESS OF LOCAL DRUG FIRMS IN THE IMPORTATION, MANUFACTURE, PACKAGING, SALE AND DISTRIBUTION OF PHARMACEUTICAL DRUGS IN THE PHILIPPINES, AND INSTITUTING FURTHER MEASURES TO LOWER THE COST OF MEDICINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Drugs Act of 2004\". The bill seeks to introduce greater state intervention through a more active and efficient regulatory system in the drug industry complemented by a more vigorous and intrusive participation of the Department of Health in the purchase and distribution of drugs to effectively influence the prevailing price schemes in the market.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D050
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-06-07, transmitted to on 2006-06-14 and received by the Senate on 2006-06-14
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AT LEAST ONE (1) SPECIAL EDUCATION (SPED) CENTER FOR EACH SCHOOL DIVISION AND AT LEAST THREE (3) SPED CENTERS IN BIG SCHOOL DIVISIONS FOR CHILDREN WITH SPECIAL NEEDS (CSNs), CREATING THE IMPLEMENTING MACHINERY THEREOF, PROVIDING GUIDELINES FOR GOVERNMENT FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE AND OTHER INCENTIVES AND SUPPORT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Special Education Act of 2004\" This bill seeks to institutionalize special education program for children with special needs (CSN). It introduces administrative reforms particularly in the structural framework of the DECS and the formulation of appropriate programs to strengthen existing polices and concerns for CSNs. To give easy access to basic education among CSNs, the measure proposes the establishment of at least one special education (SPED) center in each division school and at least three SPED centers in big schools.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05269
